EXECUTIVE ORDER 10693
Creating an E mergency  B oard T o 
Investigate D isputes  * •  Between  the 
Akron &  Barberton B elt R ailroad 
and O ther C arriers and C ertain of 
Their E mployees
WHEREAS disputes exist between the  
Akron &  Barberton Belt Railroad and  
other carriers represented by the Eastern,  
western and Southeastern Carriers'  
Conference Committees, designated in
list attached hereto and made a part  
hereof, and certain of their employees  
represented by the Brotherhood of Rail­
road Trainmen, a labor organization;  
and
WHEREAS these disputes have not  
heretofore been adjusted under the pro­
visions of the Railway Labor Act, as  
amended; and
WHEREAS these disputes, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Hoard,  
threaten substantially to interrupt inter­
state commerce to a degree such as to  
deprive the country of essential trans­
portation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 10 of  
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45  
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of  
three members, to be appointed by me, to  
investigate the said disputes. No mem­
ber of the said board shall be pecuniarily  
or otherwise interested in any organiza­
tion of employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to  
the President with respect to the said  
disputes within thirty days from the date  
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this  
date and for thirty days after the board  
has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be  
made by the Akron &  Barberton Belt  
Railroad Company and other carriers  
represented by the Eastern, Western and  
Southeastern Carriers’  Conference Com­
mittees or their employees in the condi­
tions out of which the said disputes arose.

versions.research_rationale:
EO 10693 is a single-paragraph Railway Labor Act section 10 emergency board order. Its only commands are creation of the board, a thirty-day report deadline and a recited statutory standstill. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (report deadline, option C) none of those ends the order; the first held end is the express revocation by EO 12553 on 1986-02-25 (signature date, no effective-date wording). No board report is held; no spent-fact later event is recorded. Savings: none found in EO 12553 or in the order itself. Searches: U.S. Code and eCFR number-citation searches found no hit for this order; the OFR disposition-note search lists only the EO 12553 revocation in the chain.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Checked for an earlier end: (1) the order's own terms contain a report deadline and a post-report standstill but no sunset, so the report and standstill dates are spent facts and not ends under the report-deadline ruling; (2) no extension, amendment or revocation of EO 10693 other than EO 12553 appears in the dossier chain or in the number-citation scan of held texts; the report-time extensions described in the held report (where a report is held) were stipulations approved by the President, not held instruments, and affect only the deadline; (3) a general later rule is not treated as an end, only EO 12553, which names the order by number.","independent_command_check":"The standstill is recited as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, so any no-change duty it describes arises under that statute and not only from the order; by the order's own terms it ran only to thirty days after the board's report, which was long before 1986. The order creates no continuing right, office or appropriation. No other command in the order survives the board's report.","savings_check":"The text of EO 12553 contains no savings, exception, effective-date or notwithstanding wording (the held text was searched for those terms). The board's investigation, report and the standstill were spent in the 1950s, and the order created no accrued right or later-effective duty. The statute the order invokes is not affected by revoking the order.","scope_check":"One clause covers the whole order; the order has no partial-scope command, no exception and no delayed effective date. The revocation in EO 12553 has no exception text, so it reaches the whole order."}
